Hello,
Thanks for the patch. 
I've left some comments based on my experience on other patches to this same repo.
Hi Sora, thanks for the patch! I agree with comments from @roger.gili-coscojuela@sipearl.com and @pavithrabarithaya07@gmail.com, and have left some of my own.
This should go to unreleased at the top
I guess a single changeLog comment would be good enough say - `firmware update: Add encode/decode API for downstream device update command` ?
+1 on both counts!
Done
Nitpick: Can you please use lower-case for hex constants?
Done
again here.
Done

Please remove the blank line to attach the doxygen comment to the struct.

In-fact, the comment itself doesn't add any information. I'd prefer you expand on it, or otherwise remove it.
Done

Done

Please don't abbreviate names from the spec (`device` as `dev` here). Arbitrary abbreviations make it harder to search the relevant spec for the details.

```
struct pldm_request_downstream_device_update_req
```

Please apply this consistently throughout.
Done

Again, please refrain from abbreviating:

```
uint32_t maximum_downstream_device_transfer_size;
```

Please audit the rest of the member names in all new structs.
Done
As above.
Done

Should be [in,out]
Done

The new API calls should not return PLDM completion codes anymore, instead, return negative `errno`

See https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/blob/59edcb14c996fd701e3065e3e9106bedc2d3befb/docs/checklists/changes.md?plain=1#L212

Also, the specific errors that the function returns shall be documented here.

+1

The documentation should be considered a _specification_ for the API. The implementation then needs to conform to the specification, as do the callers.

If the specification is vague then neither the caller nor the implementer can be certain about correctness. Hence explicit documentation of returned error codes. Given the state of error code handling in the implementation I think this perspective is useful 😊
Done
Again, please address the issue with abbreviation, across all new function names.
Done
Need to specify the error values the function returns and their meaning in the context of the function
Done

Done
Same as before, do not return PLDM completion codes
Done
Can we write it like this? - `if (!msg || !payload_length || !req_data)`

+1.

```
if (!req_data || !msg || !payload_length) {
```

returning PLDM error codes is no longer the way, can we use -EINVAL or some other suitable error code?

+1.

Certainly don't mix negative errno values and PLDM completion codes.
